posts.title: 2026.45: Falling Leaves (and Stocks)
posts.summary: The best Stratechery content from the week of November 2, 2026, including AI on the ballot, a Google state of the union, and China.
bullets: The recent U.S. election resulted in the largest Congressional majority for Democrats in 36 years, creating significant regulatory uncertainty for the AI infrastructure buildout.
Google experienced its first slowdown in search revenue growth in five quarters, prompting investor concern regarding the long-term sustainability of its core business model.
Analysts suggest Google's 'AI Mode' may mirror the trajectory of Facebook's Stories and Reels, potentially becoming a successful monetization engine despite initial market skepticism.
U.S.-China relations are expected to face increased volatility, with analysts predicting that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will encounter a more complex and difficult political environment in Washington.

posts.title: The Download: a humanoid cleans house and Samsung builds for the AI boom
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future. —Grace Huckins When I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning service in…
bullets: Global tech markets experienced a massive correction with $2.5 trillion in value wiped from stocks, including a $1 trillion loss among the 'Magnificent Seven' companies.
Samsung is aggressively scaling its semiconductor manufacturing capacity in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, to meet the insatiable demand for specialized memory chips required by generative AI.

Political headwinds are intensifying as Democratic lawmakers propose a national moratorium on data centers and potential pauses on advanced AI development, threatening the IPO pipelines of major firms like Anthropic.
The recent market volatility, marked by the Nasdaq's worst performance since April 2025, has sparked widespread debate among analysts regarding whether the AI investment bubble is finally bursting.

posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
HBM smuggling routes into China; Nvidia H200s held in Hong Kong; Micron pauses Taiwan fab work; Samsung expands HBM base-die capacity; Oracle-Tencent AI chip deal collapses; Bosch builds out semiconductors; S. Korea boosts AI and chip spending; Marvell-Lumentum deal draws scrutiny; more acquisitions, market reports and earnings.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Smuggling operations are bypassing U.S. export controls by packaging HBM with low-performance processors for shipment to China, where the memory is then extracted for use in AI systems.
Approximately 600,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips are currently stalled in Hong Kong as Beijing restricts imports to accelerate the adoption of domestic alternatives.
Oracle has terminated a $7 billion, five-year deal to provide Tencent with access to advanced AI chips via Southeast Asian data centers due to mounting U.S. regulatory pressure.
Samsung is reportedly expanding its HBM base-die foundry capacity, with potential 2nm production orders from Nvidia and AMD targeted for a 2030 launch in Taylor, Texas.
Bosch is restructuring its semiconductor operations to launch a dedicated division by 2028, aiming for €5 billion in annual sales by 2030 through expanded foundry and testing services.

posts.title: BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme breaches 500 km/h barrier to set new world record for production cars
posts.summary:
The Yangwang U9 Xtreme reached 503.17 km/h (312.66 miles per hour) in a top-speed challenge on public roads in Abu Dhabi.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme set a new production car speed record by reaching 503.17 km/h in Abu Dhabi.
The supercar utilizes a 1,200-volt ultra-high-voltage platform and a quad-motor system delivering a combined peak output of 2,220 kW.
Limited to 30 units globally, the vehicle is priced at over 20 million yuan, positioning it as a halo product for BYD's technological capabilities.

posts.title: Tesla pushes Shanghai plant localization to 98%, bringing joint developments with Chinese suppliers global
posts.summary:
Over the past several years, Tesla had always described the Shanghai factory's parts localization rate as "over 95%."
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Tesla's Gigafactory Shanghai has increased its parts localization rate to 98%, deepening its integration with the local Chinese supply chain.
More than 400 local tier-1 suppliers now support the plant, with over 60 of these companies integrated into Tesla's global supply network.
The facility continues to serve as a global export hub, with co-developed comfort features from the Model Y L now being rolled out to international markets including the US.
